headline_marked: [[Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro and 3 Pro approved]] as over-the-counter hearing aids in South Korea
headline: Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro and 3 Pro approved as over-the-counter hearing aids in South Korea
summary: Following US FDA approval, South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety has cleared the hearing aid feature, expanding its global rollout. The feature targets users 18+ with mild to moderate hearing loss.
details: Samsung Galaxy Buds 4 Pro and Buds 3 Pro have received approval from South Korea's Ministry of Food and Drug Safety to function as over-the-counter hearing aids. This follows earlier US FDA approval in August 2026, which designated the feature as a medical device for the region. The South Korean green light paves the way for wider international availability.

The hearing aid functionality is divided into two modules: "Hearing Test" and "Hearing Aid." The "Hearing Test" is registered as a software-based medical tool, while the Galaxy Buds themselves serve as the hardware for the OTC hearing aid.

Samsung states that this feature is designed for users aged 18 and older experiencing mild to moderate hearing loss. It utilizes NAL-NL2, a fitting technology commonly found in dedicated standalone hearing aids.

Users can conduct a clinical-grade audiometry test themselves via the Galaxy Buds app on their Samsung Galaxy phone. This 5-minute per session test covers both ears and produces an audiogram showing hearing capacity, comparable to audiologist results.

The test results categorize hearing into four levels: normal, mild, moderate, severe, or profound. Once a hearing profile is established, the Buds 4 Pro or 3 Pro can boost sound output, either on both sides or individually, to compensate for diagnosed hearing loss.

This amplification can make voices in conversations or vocals in music more audible. Advanced features like noise reduction enhance speech and help prevent further hearing loss, alongside beamforming for effective sound channeling.

The Hearing Test and Hearing Aid features are slated to arrive for US users in Q4 2026, with a broader rollout to other countries, including South Korea, expected in early 2027. Samsung's move follows Apple, which introduced similar hearing aid capabilities in its AirPods Pro 2 and Pro 3.

headline_marked: [[Nothing's mysterious AI-first device ships in December]], says CEO Carl Pei
headline: Nothing's mysterious AI-first device ships in December, says CEO Carl Pei
summary: The 'AI-native product' is described as a screen-free productivity tool that couldn't be an app, adding to the mystery surrounding its capabilities.
details: Nothing CEO Carl Pei announced on X that the company's first "AI-native product" will ship in December. This device is described as a tool built with Nothing's signature personality and care.
Pei clarified that the product will have no new screen and could not have been an app, further labeling it a "productivity tool." This description adds to the intrigue surrounding its exact nature.

Nothing has previously teased an AI-first device and mentioned plans for AI-linked smart glasses and AI-integrated earbuds. However, Pei's recent statements seem to distance this new product from typical AI wearables.

Pei noted that the industry is "hunting for its iPhone moment" with various AI companions like pendants, pins, and glasses. He expressed admiration for the boldness but indicated a different approach for Nothing's offering.
While a firm release date hasn't been announced, Nothing fans can expect more details soon. The company aims to define what makes AI part of everyone's life in a unique way.
